acceptance_condition: A proved dichotomy (growth factor 3 only on an explicitly bounded sub-family; factor >= 7 elsewhere) together with a proved sublinear or improved-constant upper bound for N(H), or a verified counterexample vertex off the slow family with a child of factor < 7.
rationale: The tree proof shows chain vertices with a=b have only 2 children and slowest growth factor 3, while ab >= 2 forces factor >= 7; quantifying the rare-slow-versus-common-fast split is the exact lever the O(H) bound needs, and the structural lemmas here make the split well-defined.
text: For the D4 sharpening: prove that any vertex with a >= 2 (equivalently, off the (1,1,c,d)-chain and its immediate children) has every child growing by factor >= 4ab-1 >= 7, and bound the number of vertices with d <= H that have a = b = 1 or ab <= 2; conclude whether N(H) = O(H^alpha) for some alpha < 1.
